title: The Codex CLI Surface
description: One codex binary, many doors: subcommands like exec/resume/review/cloud and TUI slash commands all dispatch onto the same agent loop.

steps.content: argv = [codex, exec, --json, "fix the flaky login test"]
steps.annotation: The single codex binary parses argv and dispatches on the subcommand before any model call.

steps.content: dispatch(exec) -> run_headless: resolve Config, then start the SAME agent loop the TUI uses
steps.annotation: exec / resume / review / cloud are thin wrappers that configure and launch one shared harness.
In exec mode the task is an argument; in the TUI it is a typed turn. The loop sees the same user message either way.

steps.content: I'll reproduce the flake, then patch the race.
steps.annotation: The model plans against the task, identical to an interactive turn.
The loop emits a shell function call; headless mode runs it under the resolved sandbox policy.

steps.content: 1 failed intermittently: read of token returned null
steps.annotation: The result is appended back into the conversation, exactly as in the TUI.

steps.content: The read races the write; I'll await the store before asserting.
steps.annotation: No function_call in the previous response would break the loop; here it continues.

steps.content: meanwhile, in the TUI: "/model gpt-5-codex high" starts with "/" -> intercepted as a slash command
steps.annotation: Composer text that starts with "/" is dispatched to a local command and is never sent to the model.

steps.content: dispatch(/model) -> set session { model, reasoning_effort }; /compact /diff /mcp /status resolve the same way
steps.annotation: Slash commands and subcommands share one dispatch layer over the harness.
The loop ends with a user-facing result; exec prints it (as JSON events with --json).
